partAClaim.mechanism: findProvisionView's DEFINITION branch now fully normalizes both sides via normalizeDefinedTermRef (was leading/trailing-whitespace-only). getDefinition and getTargetCurrentText unified behind one canonical resolveOperativeDefinitionEvidence primitive (amendment/operative-state.ts) with a 6-value DefinitionEvidenceStatus enum (CURRENT/KNOWN_SUPERSEDED/OPERATIVE_STATE_UNRESOLVED/AMBIGUOUS_TARGET/PARTIAL_AMENDMENT/HISTORICAL_ONLY) and an isCurrentTruth boolean gate. ToolExecutionOutcome/ToolCallLogEntry.evidenceUnresolved is set whenever a CURRENT_OPERATIVE_EVIDENCE tool call's own returned evidence is not confidently current. compile.ts pushes OPERATIVE_STATE_UNRESOLVED onto failureReasons whenever any toolCallLog entry carries evidenceUnresolved:true (forcing at least REVIEW_REQUIRED); verify.ts's determineStatus (hasUnresolvedDefinitionEvidence) forces REVIEW_REQUIRED under the identical condition before any VERIFIED_* status can be returned.
partAClaim.ownSelfDisclosedLimitation: None acknowledged regarding evidence that reaches the model WITHOUT a tool call. Part A's own testedScenarios list and its two e2e tests (compile.ts, verify.ts) both exercise ONLY the path where a getDefinition/tool call is actually made and its evidenceUnresolved flag is what carries the signal - the verify.ts e2e test in particular hand-builds a toolCallLog entry with evidenceUnresolved:true already set, which proves the CHECK works once the signal exists, but never tests whether the signal can fail to exist in the first place for a genuinely unresolved definition.

codeReadDirectly.method: Read lib/contract-model/compiler/amendment/operative-state.ts (resolveOperativeDefinitionEvidence, normalizeDefinedTermRef, buildProvisionView, getNodeSupersessionStatus), lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic/tools.ts (getDefinition, findProvisionView, getDefinitionDependencies, ToolRunner), lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic/caller.ts (RealSemanticCaller.compile, summarizeContextBundle), lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic/compile.ts (compileCovenantToIR's failureReasons wiring), lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic-verification/verify.ts (hasUnresolvedDefinitionEvidence, determineStatus), and lib/contract-model/compiler/context-retrieval/types.ts (ContextItem/CovenantContextBundle) in full at the audited commit, plus grepped every call site of getDefinition/resolveOperativeDefinitionEvidence/findProvisionView/evidenceUnresolved before writing any test.
codeReadDirectly.keyObservation1_whitespaceFixItselfHolds: normalizeDefinedTermRef (`term.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim().toLowerCase()`) is applied to BOTH sides of every comparison in resolveOperativeDefinitionEvidence and in findProvisionView's DEFINITION branch. JS's \s already covers NBSP, ideographic/en/em/narrow-no-break spaces and CR/LF, so the fix is genuinely robust against every realistic OCR/line-wrap whitespace variant tested (Group 1 below) - a zero-width space (U+200B, category Cf, outside \s) is the one residual matching gap found, but it fails SAFE (NOT_FOUND, never a false CURRENT) so it is not a safety defect of this fix.
codeReadDirectly.keyObservation2_theRealGap: ToolCallLogEntry.evidenceUnresolved (semantic/tools.ts line 423) is set ONLY inside getDefinition's own execute() body, and ONLY a tool call that actually runs ever produces a log entry at all (ToolRunner.run, called only when the model emits a tool_use block). caller.ts's own summarizeContextBundle (lines 121-135) dumps `input.contextBundle.items[].excerptText` VERBATIM into the model's very first user-turn message, with a header explicitly inviting the model to answer from it before calling any tool ('Already-gathered context... read this BEFORE requesting tools'). ContextItem (context-retrieval/types.ts) carries no operative-state/supersession field of any kind for a DEFINITION-type item - confirmed by reading the full interface. So a definition's raw, potentially stale/conflicted excerptText can reach the model's context, and therefore the model's final submission, having NEVER passed through getDefinition/resolveOperativeDefinitionEvidence at all - meaning evidenceUnresolved is never set, compile.ts's failureReasons check (`callResult.toolCallLog.some(e => e.evidenceUnresolved)`) sees an empty/uninformative toolCallLog, and verify.ts's hasUnresolvedDefinitionEvidence has literally nothing to inspect. This is a definition-side counterpart to the ALREADY-DOCUMENTED gap this codebase's own comments admit for getContextBundleComponent/getSharedCapContext's raw excerptText (semantic/tools.ts's summarizeItemWithSupersession header) - but that fix (BLOCKER-5, prior workstream) only annotates a TOOL RESPONSE that re-reads the bundle; it was never extended to the always-present INITIAL context dump every compilation attempt receives regardless of whether any tool is ever called, and Part A's OPEN-2 fix (04-definition-operative-fix.json) does not mention or touch caller.ts's summarizeContextBundle at all.

assessmentOfPartAsClaim.whatPartAGotRight: The root-cause whitespace-normalization fix (findProvisionView's DEFINITION branch, and resolveOperativeDefinitionEvidence's own both-sides-normalize discipline) is genuinely robust - confirmed under 6 fresh unicode/whitespace-irregularity constructions this audit invented independently, none of which were in Part A's own suite. The unified 6-status DefinitionEvidenceStatus/isCurrentTruth primitive is a real architectural improvement (single source of truth replacing two independently-maintained disciplines). The chained-amendment-with-interleaved-enclosing-supersession composition (Group 3) - a scenario this audit specifically invented to try to trip up the interaction between chain resolution and supersession-checking - holds correctly with no defect found. compile.ts's and verify.ts's evidenceUnresolved-forced-REVIEW_REQUIRED wiring is real and functions exactly as documented WHENEVER a getDefinition call actually happens and is logged.
assessmentOfPartAsClaim.wherePartAsClaimOverreaches: Part A's own stated design principle ('A semantic compiler using an unresolved definition may still produce candidate IR for review, but must not become trusted verified current truth solely from that definition - enforced deterministically... by threading one new boolean signal through the existing, already-built architecture') is FALSE as an unconditional guarantee: the boolean signal (evidenceUnresolved) is threaded through the TOOL-CALL path only. Neither compile.ts nor verify.ts independently re-checks a compiled rule/definition's own referenced term names against the real operativeState/resolveOperativeDefinitionEvidence - both are entirely dependent on the model having actually invoked getDefinition. caller.ts's summarizeContextBundle hands the model the same class of raw, unaudited definitional text this phase's own prior workstream already flagged as a real risk for the TOOL-response path (getContextBundleComponent/getSharedCapContext), but Part A's OPEN-2 fix neither touches nor even mentions this always-present initial-context injection point. A model need not be malicious to trigger this - the system prompt's own instruction ('Already-gathered context... read this BEFORE requesting tools') actively encourages answering from context first, which is the ordinary, cost-conscious, intended behavior this tool-use loop was designed to reward.

dispositionRationale: OPEN-2 is NOT closed. Part A's remediation correctly fixes the specific reproduction it inherited (a whitespace-irregular getDefinition query term silently missing a real on-file OperativeProvisionView and falling back to stale base-document text), and this audit's own fresh adversarial whitespace/casing/pluralization/chained-supersession constructions confirm that fix generalizes honestly with no new defect found in any of those directions. However, the downstream propagation guarantee Part A claims closes BLOCKER-5/6's full remaining scope ('a downstream compiler/verification path can no longer mark a candidate COMPLETED/VERIFIED off an unresolved definition dependency alone') does not hold end-to-end: it holds only for the code path where getDefinition is actually invoked. A definition's real, on-file CONFLICTED (or, by the same mechanism, AMBIGUOUS_TARGET/PARTIAL_AMENDMENT/KNOWN_SUPERSEDED/HISTORICAL_ONLY) status is entirely invisible to both compile.ts's failureReasons check and verify.ts's hasUnresolvedDefinitionEvidence check whenever the same term's raw excerptText already sits in the compilation's own CovenantContextBundle (Phase 2D's pre-existing, always-injected initial context, which this codebase's own comments elsewhere already admit carries no operative-state annotation) and the model answers from it without calling any tool - which its own system prompt explicitly, and correctly for cost-discipline reasons, encourages it to try first. Demonstrated end to end via the real RealSemanticCaller tool-use loop, compileCovenantToIR, and verifyCompiledCandidate: a genuinely CONFLICTED definition reaches compile status COMPLETED (zero tool calls, empty toolCallLog, failureReasons excludes OPERATIVE_STATE_UNRESOLVED) and, fed forward, verify status VERIFIED_NO_MATERIAL_GAP_FOUND/VERIFIED_WITH_NON_MATERIAL_FINDINGS - exactly the 'trusted verified current truth off an unresolved definition' outcome the fix's own design principle claims is now unreachable. Recommended remediation (not applied, per this task's read-only-on-production-code constraint): either (a) have compileCovenantToIR/verifyCompiledCandidate independently cross-check every compiled rule/definition's own referenced defined-term names (WireRule/WireDefinition's dependsOnTerms, termName, and any DEFINED_TERM_REFERENCE expression node) against a real resolveOperativeDefinitionEvidence call regardless of whether the model itself ever requested one, or (b) annotate every DEFINITION/DEFINITION_DEPENDENCY-type ContextItem Phase 2D's own retrieval pipeline builds with the same per-item operative-evidence status/isCurrentTruth signal already computed for the tool-response path, and have caller.ts's summarizeContextBundle surface it in the initial prompt so a model reading context alone is never handed unresolved evidence without the label that would make honest self-reporting possible - and, symmetrically, thread that per-item signal into evidenceUnresolved so a dishonest self-report is still deterministically caught downstream exactly as compile.ts/verify.ts already do for the tool-call path.
